instruction: I'm building a bibliography for my deep learning course. The docx file contains paper titles. Please export DBLP bibtex entries for both the Attention paper (Attention is All you Need) and the BERT paper to 'references.bib'. Use published versions, not arxiv. Separate them with blank lines.

metadata.explanation: Task requires exporting bibtex for 2 papers (Attention and BERT). Evaluator checks for both papers with partial credit: 0.5 if one found, 1.0 if both found.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator comprehensively checks all instruction requirements
Getter correctly identifies both papers using specific keyword matching: 'attention is all' for Attention paper, word boundary matching '\bbert\b' for BERT
DBLP verification implemented: checks for biburl/bibsource/url containing 'dblp.org' (lines 62-66 in getter)
Published version verification implemented: checks for absence of 'arxiv' in journal/booktitle/venue/url fields (lines 70-77 in getter)
Blank line separation verified: regex check for '\n\s*\n\s*@' pattern (line 48 in getter)
Required bibtex fields validated: checks for author and year fields (lines 80-82 in getter)
Metric applies appropriate penalties for each missing requirement: 20% for non-DBLP, 20% for arxiv, 15% for missing blank lines, 15% for missing fields
Partial credit logic is sound: base score by proportion of papers found, then penalties applied only if all papers present
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider also checking for 'organization' or 'publisher' fields in addition to author/year to ensure more complete bibtex entries
Minor: The DBLP check could be more robust by also checking the entry key format (DBLP typically uses 'DBLP:conf/...' or 'DBLP:journals/...' patterns)
